# Text contrast diagnostic controls — unresolved

Original OOXML generated by `tools/text_contrast_fixture.py`, using the project's
original automatic-table-border OPC scaffold. Eight 18pt regular text samples
pair dark blue on white with white on dark blue for Century Gothic, Arial,
Times New Roman and Harrington. The reference application opened the exact
source path and exported `native.pdf`. No font binaries or third-party templates
are included. Source and all editing exports pass transitional XML schemas.

At 384dpi, foreground coverage in each 30pt-high paragraph box, normalized
against its declared background, gives these browser/reference ink ratios:

| Font | Dark on white | White on blue | Diagnostic black mask, recolored white |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Century Gothic | 1.0074 | 1.0639 | 0.9899 |
| Arial | 0.9973 | 1.0588 | 0.9971 |
| Times New Roman | 0.9922 | 1.0731 | 0.9920 |
| Harrington | 0.9800 | 1.0879 | 0.9798 |

The private diagnostic intercepts page-canvas text drawing, draws black glyphs
into a transparent mask with the same font and transform, then applies the
requested color with source-in compositing. This narrows the issue to
color-dependent raster coverage, rather than missing fonts or a bold flag.
It is not shipped: allocating a full-page canvas for every text draw is not
an acceptable implementation. Font/position/raster residuals also remain.

This fixture records an open defect and a promising diagnostic, not a passing
native-equivalence test. A production solution still needs bounded drawing
storage, clipping/transform/outline coverage, editing regression and measured
rendering cost. Do not compensate with a template- or font-specific stroke.

Follow-up rendering experiments (none integrated): an 8 MiB bounded glyph-tile
cache preserves the improved coverage, but a 300-run native-canvas diagnostic
took 241.5ms cold and 16.6ms warm, versus direct text at 22.1ms and 5.7ms.
An offscreen-source/native-shadow approach retained the original color-dependent
ink ratios, so it does not correct the defect. A native SVG color filter gave
similar coverage to the neutral mask but took about 8.5 seconds per 300 draws
versus 21.1ms cold / 6.6ms warm direct. These measurements reject the candidates;
they are local diagnostics, not a general benchmark or a performance improvement.
The production renderer remains unchanged. Temporary experiments are retained
under scratch `work/text-contrast-{tile,shadow,filter}*` and
`work/canvas-glyph-ink-rejected.js` for future investigation.

2026-09-25 follow-up on main 74ed4caf rejects two further candidates. On an
opaque page, drawing black text with destination-out then restoring the color
with destination-over in its measured bounds avoids an offscreen glyph tile.
Its white-text ink ratios are 0.99072, 0.99780, 0.99294 and 0.98108 in the font
order above. However, the same 300-draw diagnostic measured 25.3ms cold and
43.8ms warm versus direct drawing at 9.5ms and 5.9ms. This opaque-page technique
also cannot be applied unchanged to transparent drawing surfaces.

A black glyph with the native Canvas `invert(1)` filter produces the same
coverage ratios, but costs 13,859ms cold / 15,380.6ms warm versus 9.3ms / 4.1ms
direct. These are single local diagnostic runs with a readback to flush work,
not statistically controlled benchmarks; their large cost increases do not
justify integrating either candidate. No production module was changed.
Source and PDF hashes match the original retained controls.
